references.text: The same chapter contains a parallel law about cursing one's father or mother, which also carries the death penalty as a consequence.
Repeats the prohibition against cursing one's father or mother with the death penalty, highlighting the seriousness of offenses against parents in the Mosaic Law.
Concerns a stubborn and rebellious son who does not obey his parents, and describes the procedure for handling such disobedience.
Declares a curse upon anyone who dishonors their father or mother, emphasizing the importance of honoring parents.
Warns that whoever curses their father or mother will have their lamp extinguished in darkness.
Describes the consequences for one who mocks their father and despises obeying their mother.
Jesus quotes the command to honor father and mother, referring to the death penalty for those who curse them.
Jesus cites Moses' command to honor father and mother, mentioning the death penalty for anyone who curses parents.
Describes the social and spiritual consequences (shame) of the same type of violation against parents that is forbidden in Exodus.
